title: Your First Case App
learning_objectives: Create your first PEGA application using App Studio
Understand the basic structure of a case application
Learn to define case types and basic processes
Create simple user interfaces and forms

introduction.title: Building Your First PEGA Application
introduction.text: In this tutorial, you'll create your first PEGA application from scratch using App Studio. We'll build a simple 'Service Request' application that demonstrates the fundamental concepts of case management, process design, and user interface creation. This hands-on approach will give you practical experience with PEGA's low-code development capabilities.

sections.title: Planning Your Application
sections.content: Before jumping into development, it's important to plan your application structure and understand what you're building.

application_overview.name: Service Request Application
application_overview.purpose: Handle customer service requests from submission to resolution

questions: What are the main steps in handling a service request?
Who are the different users involved?
What information needs to be collected?
What are the decision points in the process?
What priority levels should be supported?
What resolution information should be captured?
What information do agents need to see?
How should the work be organized and prioritized?
What notifications or updates are needed?

sections.title: Creating Your Application
sections.content: Let's start by creating a new application in App Studio using the guided application wizard.

steps.title: Launch App Studio
steps.description: Access App Studio from your PEGA environment and start the application creation process.
detailed_steps: Log into your PEGA Personal Edition environment
From the main navigation, click on 'App Studio'
You'll see the App Studio welcome screen with options to create or open applications
Click 'Create new app' or the '+' button to start the application wizard
tips: If this is your first time in App Studio, take the guided tour
Make sure you're in the correct environment (Personal Edition)
Keep your browser window maximized for the best experience

steps.title: Configure Application Details
steps.description: Use the application wizard to define basic application information and structure.
detailed_steps: Enter 'Service Request' as your application name
Add a description: 'Customer service request management application'
Select 'Customer Service' as the application template (if available)
Choose your organization name or use the default
Click 'Create' to generate the application structure

configuration_options.template: Customer Service (or Generic if not available)

steps.title: Review Generated Structure
steps.description: Examine the application structure that PEGA has created for you.
what_to_expect: Application explorer showing your new application
Default case type created based on your application name
Basic application structure with standard components
Navigation panel showing available development tools
key_components: Case types - The main work units in your application
Processes - The workflow steps for handling cases
Data model - The information structure for your cases
User interface - The forms and screens users will interact with

sections.title: Defining Your Case Type
sections.content: The case type is the heart of your PEGA application. It defines the structure and lifecycle of the work you're managing.

case_type_basics.definition: A case type represents a unit of work that progresses through various stages until completion. In our example, each service request is a case.

configuration_steps.title: Access Case Type Settings
configuration_steps.description: Navigate to your case type configuration in App Studio.
actions: In the Application Explorer, find your case type (likely named 'Service Request')
Click on the case type to open its configuration
You'll see tabs for different aspects: Settings, Stages, Fields, etc.

configuration_steps.title: Configure Basic Settings
configuration_steps.description: Set up the fundamental properties of your case type.

settings.icon: Choose an appropriate icon (e.g., headset or support icon)

configuration_steps.title: Define Case Stages
configuration_steps.description: Set up the major phases that cases will progress through.

recommended_stages.purpose: Collect request details and validate information
Assess request and determine appropriate handling

recommended_stages.description: Active work on resolving the request
recommended_stages.purpose: Perform necessary actions to address the request
Confirm resolution and close the case

sections.title: Adding Data Fields
sections.content: Define the data fields that will store information about each service request case.

data_modeling_approach.principle: Start with essential fields and add more as needed

fields.name: AssignedTo
fields.description: Agent assigned to handle the request

fields.name: ResolutionDetails
fields.description: Details about how the request was resolved

adding_fields_steps.description: In your case type configuration, click on the 'Fields' tab
actions: Click 'Add field' to create new data fields
Enter the field name and select the appropriate type
Configure validation rules and requirements
Set default values if applicable
Create field groups for related information
Drag and drop fields to reorder them
Set up field dependencies if needed
Preview how fields will appear in forms

sections.title: Designing the Process Flow
sections.content: Create the business process that defines how service requests move through the system.
process_design_principles: Keep the initial process simple and straightforward
Focus on the main path first, add exceptions later
Use clear, descriptive names for process steps
Consider who performs each step and what they need

basic_process_flow.description: A simple linear process for handling service requests

steps.description: Customer or agent enters request details
steps.form: Request submission form with customer and request fields

steps.description: Agent reviews and categorizes the request
steps.form: Review form showing request details and assignment options

steps.description: Assigned agent works on resolving the request
steps.form: Work form for updating status and adding resolution details

creating_process_steps.title: Access Process Designer
creating_process_steps.description: Navigate to the process design interface in App Studio.
actions: In your case type, click on the 'Processes' tab
You'll see a visual process designer with a default flow
The designer shows the current process steps and connections

creating_process_steps.title: Add Process Steps
creating_process_steps.description: Create the individual steps in your process flow.
actions: Click on the '+' or 'Add step' button
Choose 'Assignment' as the step type for user tasks
Enter a descriptive name for each step
Connect steps using the flow connectors

creating_process_steps.title: Configure Step Details
creating_process_steps.description: Set up the specifics for each process step.
configuration_items: What form or interface to use

sections.title: Creating User Interfaces
sections.content: Design the forms and screens that users will interact with during the case lifecycle.
ui_design_principles: Keep forms simple and focused on the task at hand
Use clear labels and helpful instructions
Consider the user's workflow and context

form_types_needed.purpose: Collect initial request information from customer
form_types_needed.layout: Single column with logical field grouping

form_types_needed.purpose: Allow agents to review and categorize requests
form_types_needed.layout: Two-column layout showing request details and work fields

form_types_needed.purpose: Enable agents to work on and update requests
form_types_needed.layout: Focus on work fields with request context visible

creating_forms_steps.title: Access UI Designer
creating_forms_steps.description: Navigate to the user interface design tools.
actions: In your case type, click on the 'Views' or 'UI' tab
You'll see options to create and edit forms
App Studio may have created default forms based on your fields

creating_forms_steps.title: Design Form Layouts
creating_forms_steps.description: Create intuitive and efficient form layouts.
design_steps: Drag fields from the field palette onto the form canvas
Arrange fields in logical groups and order
Add section headers to organize related fields
Preview the form to see how it will appear to users

creating_forms_steps.title: Associate Forms with Process Steps
creating_forms_steps.description: Connect your forms to the appropriate process steps.
actions: Go back to your process designer
Click on each process step to configure it
Select the appropriate form for each step
Test the flow to ensure forms appear correctly

sections.title: Testing Your Application
sections.content: Before deploying your application, it's important to test it thoroughly to ensure it works as expected.

focus_areas: Basic functionality - Can you create and process cases?
Data validation - Are required fields enforced?
Process flow - Do cases move through stages correctly?
User experience - Are forms intuitive and efficient?

testing_steps.title: Preview Your Application
testing_steps.description: Use App Studio's preview feature to test your application.
actions: Look for a 'Preview' or 'Run' button in App Studio
This will open your application in a new tab or window
You can interact with your application as an end user would

testing_steps.title: Create Test Cases
testing_steps.description: Create several test cases to verify functionality.

test_scenarios.description: Create a case and process it through all stages successfully
steps: Submit a new service request with all required information
Add work notes and resolution details

test_scenarios.description: Test field validation and error handling
steps: Try to submit a request with missing required fields
Verify that appropriate error messages appear

test_scenarios.description: Test cases with different priority levels
steps: Create requests with different priority levels
Verify that priority affects case handling appropriately
Test any priority-based routing or SLAs

testing_steps.title: Review and Refine
testing_steps.description: Based on testing results, make improvements to your application.
common_improvements: Adjust form layouts for better usability

sections.title: Deploying and Sharing
sections.content: Once you're satisfied with your application, you can deploy it for others to use.

deployment_options.description: Keep the application in your Personal Edition environment for continued learning and experimentation.
If working in a team environment, you can share your application with colleagues for review and collaboration.
deployment_options.use_case: Team development, peer review, collaborative improvement

deployment_options.description: For real applications, deploy to a production environment following your organization's deployment processes.

next_development_steps: Implement advanced routing and assignment logic
Create reports and dashboards for monitoring
Implement advanced security and access controls

summary.title: What You've Accomplished
achievements: Created your first PEGA application from scratch
Defined a case type with appropriate stages and fields
Designed a basic business process flow
Tested your application to ensure it works correctly
Gained hands-on experience with App Studio's capabilities
key_concepts_learned: Case types represent units of work in PEGA
Process flows define how work moves through the system
Data fields store the information needed for each case
User interfaces provide the means for users to interact with cases
Testing is essential to ensure application quality

next_steps.title: What's Next?
next_steps.text: Congratulations on creating your first PEGA application! Now that you understand the basics of case application development, you can explore more advanced topics like data modeling, complex user interfaces, and business rules.
practice_suggestions: Enhance your Service Request application with additional features
Create a different type of application (e.g., Employee Onboarding)
Experiment with different field types and validation rules
Try creating more complex process flows with decision points
